sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Divakar Rai Sharma
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,Acting Chief Justice
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for a mandamus commanding the respondents to exempt Gata No.163, area 0.0490 hectares, Village-Tah Tajpur, Tehsil-Sadar, District Bareilly from acquisition proceedings initiated vide notifications dated 20.12.2003 and 09.12.2004 issued under Sections 4 and 6, respectively of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
and to decide representation of the petitioner dated 15.05.2023 for exempting the said land from the acquisition proceedings.

2. The facts which are not in dispute are as follows:-
(a). The State-respondents had acquired, inter alia, 0.114 hectares of Gata No.163 by issuing notification under Section 4 of the Act dated 20.12.2003 and under Section 6 dated 09.12.2004.

entities.text: Tula Ram vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The possession of the entire land was taken on 27.10.2006 and the award was made on 15.05.2013.
The petitioner had received the entire compensation amount for the acquired land.
3. The case of the petitioner is that the respondents had constructed a by-pass road over the acquired land.

However, an area measuring 0.0490 hectares had remained unutilized and,
therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said land being exempted from the acquisition proceedings under Section 48 of the Act.
4.

Shri Divakar Rai Sharma, learned counsel appearing for N.H.A.I is in receipt of instructions in compliance of the previous order and the same has been placed on record alongwith possession memo, copy of the award and documents relating to payment of entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
A complete set of documents has also been handed-over to learned counsel for the petitioner in Court.

5. Shri Divakar Rai Sharma, learned counsel for N.H.A.I submitted that since possession of entire land was taken and compensation was also paid to the petitioner for the entire land and, therefore,
Section 48 of the Act would not be attracted.
6.
We find force in the submission of Shri Divakar Rai Sharma.
Under Section 48(1), the Government can withdraw from acquisition of any land, of which, possession has not been taken.
In the instant case, admittedly, possession of entire land was taken.
Not only that, the petitioner had also withdrawn the entire compensation amount.
Consequently, provisions of Section 48 of the Act would not get attracted.
7. The petition lacks merit and is dismissed.
